title: 467. Sets, Logic, Reasoning & Proof: Set Cardinality
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Find the cardinality of a set given by listing.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{2,4,6,8,10\}\)?
questions.explanation: The cardinality is the number of elements. The set lists the five elements \(2,4,6,8,10\), so its cardinality is \(5\). The number \(10\) is the largest element, not the number of elements.
questions.hint: Count the elements; do not use their values.

questions.learningObjective: State the cardinality of the empty set.
questions.question: What is \(|\varnothing|\)?
questions.explanation: The empty set has no elements, so its cardinality is \(0\). The value \(1\) is the cardinality of a set with one element, such as \(\{\varnothing\}\).
questions.hint: Count how many objects lie between the braces of \(\{\ \}\).

questions.concept: Cardinality of a set containing the empty set
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the empty set from a set whose only element is the empty set.
questions.question: What is \(|\{\varnothing\}|\)?
questions.explanation: The set \(\{\varnothing\}\) has one element, namely the empty set. So its cardinality is \(1\). It is not the empty set, whose cardinality is \(0\).
questions.hint: Count the objects between the outer braces, whatever those objects are.

questions.learningObjective: Find the cardinality of a listing that repeats elements.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{1,2,2,3,3,3\}\)?
questions.explanation: Repeated entries name the same element. The distinct elements are \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\), so the cardinality is \(3\). The number \(6\) counts the written entries rather than the distinct elements.

questions.concept: Cardinality of a set of consecutive integers
questions.learningObjective: Count the integers in a closed interval.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{x\in\mathbb{Z}\mid -5\le x\le 5\}\)?
questions.explanation: The number of integers from \(a\) to \(b\) inclusive is \(b-a+1\). Here \(5-(-5)+1=11\). The value \(10\) omits the \(+1\), which accounts for including both endpoints (or equivalently for the element \(0\)).
questions.hint: Use the count \(b-a+1\) for the integers from \(a\) to \(b\) inclusive.

questions.concept: Cardinality with a set as an element
questions.learningObjective: Count the elements of a set when one element is itself a set.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{1,\{2,3\},4\}\)?
questions.explanation: The elements are \(1\), the set \(\{2,3\}\), and \(4\). The inner set counts as a single element, so the cardinality is \(3\). Counting \(2\) and \(3\) separately gives \(4\), but they are elements of the inner set, not of the outer one.
questions.hint: Count only the top-level elements, separated by commas outside the inner braces.

questions.concept: Cardinality of a set of divisors
questions.learningObjective: Find the number of positive divisors of an integer.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of the set of positive divisors of \(12\)?
questions.explanation: The positive divisors of \(12\) are \(1,2,3,4,6,12\). There are \(6\) of them. Forgetting that \(1\) or \(12\) itself is a divisor gives \(5\).
questions.hint: List the divisors in pairs whose product is \(12\).

questions.concept: Cardinality of a set of pairs
questions.learningObjective: Count the ordered pairs formed from two small sets.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{(a,b)\mid a\in\{1,2\},\ b\in\{7,8,9\}\}\)?
questions.explanation: Each of the \(2\) choices for \(a\) can be combined with each of the \(3\) choices for \(b\), giving \(2\cdot 3=6\) ordered pairs. Adding instead of multiplying gives \(5\), which is incorrect.
questions.hint: For each choice of the first component, count the choices of the second.

questions.learningObjective: Count the elements of a set built from nested empty sets.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\},\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}\}\)?
questions.explanation: The top-level elements are \(\varnothing\), \(\{\varnothing\}\), and \(\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}\). These are three different sets, with \(0\), \(1\), and \(2\) elements respectively, so the cardinality is \(3\).
questions.hint: The three top-level elements have different numbers of elements, so they are different sets.

questions.learningObjective: Count the integers satisfying a strict quadratic inequality.
questions.question: What is the cardinality of \(\{n\in\mathbb{Z}\mid n^2<30\}\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(5^2=25<30\) and \(6^2=36>30\), the condition holds exactly for \(-5\le n\le 5\). That is \(5-(-5)+1=11\) integers. Counting only \(0,1,2,3,4,5\) gives \(6\), which forgets the negative integers.
questions.hint: Find the largest integer whose square is below \(30\), then include its negative counterparts.
